newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile arrests five in connection with drug lord.
newsitem.headline: Chile arrests five in connection with drug lord.

text.p: Chile said on Monday its police arrested five people, including a brother of a senator, in connection with activities of the late Mexican drug lord, Amado Carrillo Fuentes.
The head of Chile's antidrugs agency, Mario Mallea, told reporters that four Chilean men and one Mexican woman were detained under racketeering charges.

Among those arrested was Hernan Errazuriz Talavera, a lawyer and brother of center-right senator Francisco Javier Errazuriz, a former presidential candidate and member of one of Chile's oldest families.
According to Mallea, the people detained had either advised or aided Carrillo in his bid to establish residency in Chile before he died in Mexico on July 4.
Carrillo spent nearly three months here early this year, buying luxurious houses, apartments and cars for himself and his lieutenants.
Mallea said Carrillo's drug trafficking organization, the Juarez Cartel, had decided to fall back to Chile due to the growing pressure they felt in their own territory.

The Mexican gangsters had surveyed several countries since 1996 and chose Chile because of its stable economy, its open markets and its proximity to Bolivia and Peru, the world's biggest producers of coca leaves.
Coca is used to make cocaine. Carrillo's cartel dominated the smuggling of that drug into the United States.
The Mexican woman, Marta Laura Rodriguez, was identified as the wife of Manuel de Jesus Bitar, one of Carrillo's sidekicks.
The other men arrested were real estate agent Jose Agustin Ramirez, money dealer Javier Ventura and chauffeur Edgardo Jimenez.
Mallea said he believed other Mexicans who had come in with Carrillo had fled the country, although he could not assure it because they used false identities.
After arriving in March from neighboring Argentina, Carrillo ensconced himself in one of Santiago's swankiest neighborhoods and bought a bullet-proof BMW car.

Over the next few weeks he went on a long tour to Chile's scenic south with his cronies, spent holidays at the Vina del Mar seaside resort and threw lavish parties complete with Mexican mariachi bands.
Carrillo traveled in June to Cuba and the following month he died in Mexico while undergoing massive plastic surgery.
